summary: Mount Rainier stone shelter (1916), then a D-6 cupola cabin (1927-28); abandoned 1942, removed or destroyed about 1947-48; little or nothing remains.

events.note: Stone shelter with an outside firefinder; registry, firelookout.com and Willhite say 1916; a 1917 newspaper item calls the stations recently built
Park Service reports for 1918-19 say fires were located and reported from the station

Rice N. Anderson named primary lookout; a storm-started set of eighteen fires near Randle was spotted from the station

resolved_conflicts.explanation: Registry, firelookout.com and Willhite give 1916. A 1917 newspaper item calls the stations recently built and a 1927 item calls the stone house built ten years earlier. The record uses 1916 and the story notes the 1917 item.
Willhite and an April 1927 newspaper item put the D-6 cabin in 1927 (the item says it would replace the stone house that season). The registry and firelookout.com say about 1928.

Registry: removed sometime after 1942. firelookout.com: destroyed in 1948. Willhite: the Park Service maybe asked for removal about 1947, and he reports an unconfirmed rumor of burning. The record uses the registry's 'removed or destroyed after 1942' wording.

notes_for_editor: The WebSearch budget for this run was used up before the search step, so the story rests on the four cited pages only. Those pages quote period newspapers and Park Service reports, which are not checked against originals. Access rules were not found, so no access or visit key is set. No photos were added. The brief lists the agency as NPS; the Weebly quotes show the Forest Service staffed the station in the 1920s. The 1916/1917 build year and the 1927/1928 cabin year are both shown in the story as source disagreements.
